newsitem.title: GERMANY: Six killed, 15 hurt in freak German rail accident.
newsitem.headline: Six killed, 15 hurt in freak German rail accident.

text.p: Six people were killed and 15 injured in a rail accident near Frankfurt on Saturday when a 15 metre (50 Foot) long iron pipe twisted off a freight train and sliced open a passing train packed with passengers, police said.
A spokesman said the accident happened shortly before 9 a.m. (0700 GMT) near the town of Stadtallendorfs, 80 km (50 miles) north of Frankfurt.
All six were aged between 17 and 40. One of the three women killed was from Ghana and one was from Sweden. Two of the three men killed were from Berlin and one was from nearby Giessen.

Three of the injured were in critical condition. Many of the passengers were youths who were sitting in the lower level of the double-decker regional train that was headed for Kassel from Frankfurt. Several school groups were on board.

"We heard the people screaming and ran immediately over here," said Thorsten Mueller, who was playing soccer nearby with a group of friends. "There was blood and broken glass everywhere. It was brutal. I have never seen anything like this."
Other witnesses who hurried to the scene reported hearing a loud bang followed by cries from injured.
"It was a really horrible bang," said one woman who lives nearby.
The lower level of the train car was completely ripped open by the iron pipe and newspapers, lunch bags, thermos bottles, fruit, and blood-soaked clothing were strewn about the floor.
Hans Eichel, the premier of the Hesse state where the accident happened, hurried to the scene and said quick first aid measures applied by other passengers and nearby residents helped save lives.

"It is a dreadful accident and a terrible day for families who have lost someone," Eichel said. "We hope that there will be no more deaths. We are most grateful to the passengers and neighbours who helped to save lives with first aid."
It was not immediately clear how the gas pipe broke loose from the freight train, which was travelling in the opposite direction.

The 1.2 metre d (four foot) diameter pipe weighing six tonnes crashed into the last car of the oncoming train and sliced open the lower level of the two-storey car. Two other pipes had rolled off the train nearby and had broken several birch trees.
"The cause is still unknown," said Peter Muenchschwander, spokesman for German rail at the scene. "The police and state prosecutors office are investigating."
Investigators said there were long scratches caused by the pipe in two cars immediately preceded the ill-fated final car. The two trains came to a stop about 500 metres apart after the collision.

The busy Frankfurt-Kassel line was expected to be closed all day, a spokesman for German rail said. The train was full of passengers taking advantage of special low weekend tariffs. There were about 300 people on board, authorities said.
A German rail spokesman said he knew of no other such serious post-war accidents resulting from materials falling off a freight train.
